area: Spike S4, WP 3.4 (io/LocalServer completed) and WP 3.5 step 1 (the base built, published and backed up)
summary: M1's minimal local server already chooses DBCHANGE_SQL, then the container via ~/.dbchange/sql.env, then LocalDB (io/LocalServer.cs:183-189). It names and registers copies as dbchange_<host>_<pid>_<rand> in .dbchange/copies.json under a lock (io/LocalServer.cs:223-235, 329-345; kernel/Target.cs:126-132). It waits 180 s on CREATE and DROP (io/LocalServer.cs:40, 303-307) and drops through SINGLE_USER WITH ROLLBACK IMMEDIATE after ClearPool, on an unpooled master connection (io/LocalServer.cs:32-33, 71-75). It refuses a server on an environment's host with exit 9 (io/LocalServer.cs:260-273; VerbExitTests.cs:65) and stamps the container's image digest into Server (io/LocalServer.cs:84-118; io/SqlServer.cs:719-722). Missing: the first-connect retry, the sweep (only the test fixture sweeps, by dead pid, SqlServerFixture.cs:120-136), backup and restore into .dbchange/cache/, io pulling or starting the container, a version check, any S4 test, and every part of WP 3.5 step 1. Two facts change the plan's assumptions. First, windows-latest is now windows-2025-vs2026 with LocalDB 17.0.4025.3, not 16.x (job 117856550219 of run 39188714136). Second, a probe here on the container (SQL Server 16.0.4295.3, DacFx 170.5.96, 300 tables, run while a fixture run shared the server) took 35.3 s to publish from scratch and 1.1 s to restore, so the base cache should restore rather than publish. Budget: io is at 5,203 of 6,400 and this area adds about 300 lines. LocalServer.cs would reach about 500 lines, so the cache half belongs in a partial file.

items.name: Spike S4: CREATE, publish, BACKUP, RESTORE and DROP of a 300-table copy, timed in CI on the container and on LocalDB

Probe in scratch on the container (16.0.4295.3 Developer, DacFx 170.5.96, 300 OutSystems-shaped tables, each with PK, FK to the previous table, index, defaults and check): model and package 4.2 s, CREATE 0.23 s, publish from scratch 35.3 s, republish with nothing to do 9.3 s, BACKUP 0.39 s, RESTORE WITH MOVE 1.1 s, DROP 0.06 to 0.08 s. items.name: WP 3.4: DROP through SINGLE_USER WITH ROLLBACK IMMEDIATE, and ClearPool, on an unpooled master connection
items.evidence: Unmake (io/LocalServer.cs:32-33) wraps the DROP in `IF DB_ID(@name) IS NOT NULL … SET SINGLE_USER WITH ROLLBACK IMMEDIATE; DROP DATABASE`. Drop (:71-75) calls SqlConnection.ClearPool on the copy's own pooled connection, then runs Unmake through Run with Catalog=master and Pooled=false (:303-307). The WP's wording, 'ClearPool on an unpooled master connection', reads oddly: ClearPool on an unpooled connection does nothing. The code clears the copy database's pool and drops over unpooled master, which is the right reading.

items.evidence: No retry exists. LocalServer.Run (io/LocalServer.cs:303-307) calls SqlServer.Query once, and Query (io/SqlServer.cs:383-437) opens one connection with no retry. ConnectTimeoutSeconds = 15 (io/ConnectionString.cs:57). The Facsimile's TLC-10 (archive/v2/ssdt-agent/facsimile/cases/70-process.md, 'LocalDB's first connection times out, and is retried') and TARGET.md:252 call for one retry. The fast test TargetTests.A_local_server_that_does_not_answer_names_ci_sql_up_and_leaves_no_registry_row (TargetTests.cs:645) uses a closed port, which refuses at once, so a retry keeps it fast. The remedy for an unreachable copy names ci/sql.sh even when the server is LocalDB (io/SqlServer.cs:116-117).
items.remaining:
In io/LocalServer.cs:
- Add `internal static Result<T> Connected<T>(Func<Result<T>> attempt, TimeSpan pause)`. When the attempt fails with code server.unreachable and no statement of this process has yet reached the local server, wait `pause` (a named constant, FirstConnectPause = 2 s) and try once more. Any other error, or a second failure, returns as it is.
- Keep a static flag, set with Interlocked after the first successful statement, so later statements are never retried.
- Wrap Run's SqlServer.Query call in it.

In io/SqlServer.cs Database.ErrorOf (:116-117), give a copy on a LocalDB host (Host.LocalDb) the remedy `sqllocaldb start MSSQLLocalDB`, then run dbchange doctor.
testsFirst: Io.Tests, fast: "The first connect to the local server is retried once and a refusal is not". It passes a counting attempt to LocalServer.Connected with a zero pause. Two server.unreachable failures give two attempts and server.unreachable. A server.denied gives one attempt. Unreachable then Ok gives Ok. After one success, a later unreachable is not retried.

items.name: WP 3.4: the sweep drops only this host's registered names older than a day; done when a killed run is swept by the next
items.evidence: io has no sweep. The only sweep is the test fixture's SqlServerFixture.SweepAsync (tests/Io.Tests/SqlServerFixture.cs:120-136). It reads sys.databases, not the registry, and drops this machine's CopyName-shaped databases whose pid is not running. io cannot do that check: io/BannedSymbols.txt bans System.Diagnostics.Process outside io/Command. VALUES.md:76 O5 cites `Io.Tests: "a killed run is swept by the next"` as not held yet, WP 3.4. Its text says the sweep drops only this host's registered names older than a day. That conflicts with the done-when 'a killed run is swept by the next': a run killed less than a day ago is not swept. Precedent for a holder-lock sweep: io/Git.At sweeps worktrees no running process holds (DECISIONS.md:37; io/LocalState.cs:55-56). tests/Io.Tests/DbChangeProcess.cs:16-41 already runs this test assembly as a child program, with a `lock` mode.
items.remaining:
In io/LocalServer.cs, add `public static Result<IReadOnlyList<CopyName>> Sweep(string repositoryRoot, SqlServer.QueryLog log)`, which calls `internal static Result<IReadOnlyList<CopyName>> Sweep(string repositoryRoot, SqlServer.QueryLog log, DateTimeOffset now, Func<Result<string>> chosen)`.

The selection is a pure function `internal static IReadOnlyList<CopyName> Stale(IEnumerable<JsonObject> rows, string machine, Kernel.ServerName server, DateTimeOffset now)`. A row is stale when all of these hold:
- its name parses as a CopyName (CopyName.Of);
- name.Machine == CopyName.Make(Environment.MachineName, 0, 0).Machine;
- its server equals the local server as it is now. A row on another server cannot be dropped from here and is left;
- its created is more than one day before now. A row with no created or an unparseable one counts as old.

Drop each stale copy as Drop does: ClearPool, then Run(copy, "DROP DATABASE", Unmake, log), then remove its row through Change.

Call Sweep at the start of `Create(repositoryRoot, server, log, resolve)` (io/LocalServer.cs:223), after R15 clears the server and before the new row is written. Return its error rather than swallow it.

Tests: add a `copy <repository root>` mode to DbChangeProcess (tests/Io.Tests/DbChangeProcess.cs). It makes a copy through LocalServer.Create on the server DBCHANGE_SQL names, passed in the child's environment and never on its command line. It prints the copy's name and waits on stdin.

If the operator prefers a killed copy to go at once: give each copy a holder FileLock at .dbchange/copies/<name>.lock, held by the creating process until Drop and released by the operating system when it dies, the worktree precedent. The sweep would take that lock with a zero timeout. That rewrites O5's text and needs a decision line.

Then change VALUES.md:76 O5's last cell to `Io.Tests: "a killed run is swept by the next"` and regenerate LAWS.md with ci/laws.sh.
testsFirst: Io.Tests, fast: "The sweep chooses only this host's copies on this server registered more than a day ago", over LocalServer.Stale with rows from two machines, two servers, ages 23 h and 25 h, and one row without created.

Io.Tests, fixture, Trait Value O5: "A killed run is swept by the next". It starts DbChangeProcess `copy`, reads the name and kills the process; the database and row remain. It then calls Sweep with now set to the row's created plus one day and one minute; the database and row are gone, while another machine's row and a fresh row remain.

items.name: WP 3.4: backup and restore into .dbchange/cache/
items.evidence: No BACKUP or RESTORE exists in io: rg finds none in io/*.cs. io/LocalState.cs:21-106 names no cache folder. V3_MILESTONES.md:276 maps the Facsimile's caches to `.dbchange/cache/`. The container's SQL Server runs as uid 10001 (mssql) and writes only inside the container. Its InstanceDefaultBackupPath is /var/opt/mssql/data, and ci/sql.sh:49 mounts no host folder. So BACKUP TO DISK cannot reach the repository's .dbchange/cache/ directly. LocalDB runs as the user and can write there. A DBCHANGE_SQL server on another machine writes to its own disk. A Windows SQL Server service usually cannot write to the user's folder (Msg 3201). CapabilityTests.Nothing_but_LocalServer_makes_a_Copy (CapabilityTests.cs:94-102, with CopyConstructor().Single() at :125) requires one internal Copy constructor, called only from inside LocalServer. A partial class LocalServer in another file still counts as inside.
items.remaining:
New file io/LocalServer.Cache.cs, declared `public static partial class LocalServer`. Make the class in io/LocalServer.cs partial as well.

LocalState additions:
- `Cache` (.dbchange/cache)
- `CacheEntry(key)` (cache/<key>.bak)
- `CacheMarker(key)` (cache/<key>.json)
- `CacheLock(key)` (cache/<key>.lock)
The folder is made through LocalState.Made, so .dbchange/.gitignore stands beside it.

Backup: `internal static Result<string> Backup(SqlServer.Copy copy, string entry, SqlServer.QueryLog log)`. Choose where the server writes:
- When LocalServer.Image(copy) is not null (the container serves): back up to `<InstanceDefaultBackupPath>/dbchange-<key>-<rand>.bak` inside the container, then `docker cp dbchange-sql:<that> <entry>`, then `docker exec dbchange-sql rm -f <that>`. Both run through Command, with a named CopyTimeout of 180 s.
- When the server's host is this machine (LocalDB, or localhost without the container): back up to the entry path itself.
- Otherwise: error cache.unavailable naming the server, which the caller turns into a note and builds uncached.
The statement is `BACKUP DATABASE @name TO DISK = @path WITH COPY_ONLY, INIT, FORMAT, CHECKSUM`, with both parameters as variables and no dynamic SQL needed. Do not use COMPRESSION, which LocalDB and Express refuse. Run it through Run with the 180 s timeout. Msg 3201 or 3013 becomes cache.unwritable naming the folder.

Restore: `internal static Result<SqlServer.Copy> Restore(string repositoryRoot, string entry, SqlServer.QueryLog log)`. It makes a new registered copy exactly as Create does: R15 check, sweep, the row written first and removed on failure. Factor Create's body so the statement that makes the database is a parameter, Make or the restore.
- For the container, stage the .bak with `docker cp`. Make sure uid 10001 can read it: chmod 0644, or `docker exec -u 0 … chown mssql`.
- Run RESTORE FILELISTONLY FROM DISK = @path for the logical names and types.
- Then RESTORE DATABASE <the new name> FROM DISK = @path WITH MOVE <each logical file> TO <InstanceDefaultDataPath or InstanceDefaultLogPath><name>_<file_id>.<mdf|ldf|ndf>, CHECKSUM. Build the statement as dynamic SQL with N'…' literals escaped by REPLACE. QUOTENAME returns NULL past 128 characters, and file paths can be longer.
- Delete the staged file.

The restored copy has a new dbchange_<host>_<pid>_<rand> name and a row in copies.json. Fingerprint.Of of the two extracted models is equal, and the .bak is under .dbchange/cache/. Both are dropped.

items.name: WP 3.5 step 1: the database named from its fingerprints (§4 row 13)
items.evidence:
V3_MILESTONES.md:318 (§4 row 13) names the synthetic copy `dbchange_synthetic_<schema>_<evidence>_<seed>_<tier>[_<existing-data>]`. The re-cut (V3_MILESTONES.md:555-575, §17 item 20, pending) drops evidence and seed, and the only tier is existing-data. DECISIONS.md:86 fixes the `[_<existing-data>]` suffix. VALUES.md:77 O6 still lists 'schema, evidence, seed, tier and existing data'.

What the plan leaves unsettled:
- Width: Fingerprint.ToString is 64 hex (kernel/Fingerprint.cs:122). Two of them plus the prefix is about 150 characters, past SQL Server's 128-character sysname, so they must be cut. Precedent: Ssdt.Build cuts to the first 16 digits (io/Ssdt.cs:217-218).
- Which inputs 'schema' covers: the package alone, or also profile, DacFx and server. The Facsimile's base key, D5, covers the dacpac, reference data, options, tool, DacFx and LocalDB versions (archive/v2/ssdt-agent/facsimile/ARCHITECTURE.md:227-237).
- Host: there is none, so two machines on one DBCHANGE_SQL, or two clones on one machine each with their own .dbchange/ lock, collide on one fingerprint name.
- The suffix: `--existing-data` needs WP 2.1's ExistingData (M2, which waits on the operator's go). Only Provenance.ExistingData exists, as a Fingerprint? (kernel/Provenance.cs:40).
- Name clash: CopyName's grammar (kernel/Target.cs:100) is `[a-z0-9_]`, and the fixture's sweep (SqlServerFixture.cs:131) drops whatever parses as one. A synthetic name must never parse as a CopyName.
- CapabilityTests.cs:125 requires Copy to keep one internal constructor, which takes a CopyName (io/SqlServer.cs:180). A fingerprint-named Copy therefore needs that constructor generalized (its uses: DacFx.cs:174 and LocalServer.cs:74, 229, 234, 306).
items.remaining:
Proposed name for the step-1 synthetic copy: `dbchange_synthetic_<16 hex of the base's fingerprint>_existing-data[_<16 hex of the ExistingData fingerprint>]`. Example: dbchange_synthetic_0123456789abcdef_existing-data_fedcba9876543210, 69 characters.
- The base's fingerprint is the cache key: Fingerprint.Of over canonical text of the package model's fingerprint (pre- and post-deploy scripts and refactorlog included, so the seeds count), the profile's Fingerprint, DacFx.Version, Server version, compatibility level and image, and the dbchange version. A profile, DacFx or server change then gives a new name.
- The hyphen in `existing-data` keeps the name outside CopyName's grammar, so no per-process sweep ever drops it.
- Defer the kernel type (`SyntheticCopyName`, readonly record struct in kernel/Target.cs beside CopyName, with Make(Fingerprint base, Fingerprint? existingData), Of(subject, text), and ToString; about 35 lines) to the restore that plants the synthetic copy (steps 2 to 8). Step 1 can build its base in a registered disposable copy, as the next item says.
- Record the settled grammar as one paragraph correcting §4 row 13 and VALUES.md O6, with a decision line.
items.question: §4 row 13 names the synthetic copy dbchange_synthetic_<schema>_<evidence>_<seed>_<tier>[_<existing-data>]. The re-cut leaves <schema>_<tier>[_<existing-data>], and full fingerprints push that past SQL Server's 128-character limit. May it read dbchange_synthetic_<16 hex of the base's fingerprint (package, profile, DacFx, server)>_existing-data[_<16 hex of the existing data's>], with no host, recorded as a correction to row 13?
testsFirst: Kernel.Tests, fast, when the name lands: "A synthetic copy's name carries its base's and its existing data's fingerprints and never reads as a disposable copy's name". A CsCheck property: Of(Make(b, e).ToString()) equals Make(b, e); CopyName.Of fails on every made name; the length is at most 128.

items.name: WP 3.5 step 1: the base built at a ref, published under the pipeline's profile, backed up into .dbchange/cache/ under a lock, and reached again from the cache
items.evidence:
There is no io/SyntheticCopy.cs, and Target.SyntheticCopy resolves to 'synthetic-copy.not-built' (io/SqlServer.cs:219-220). What exists to build on:
- FileLock.Take(path, timeout): io/FileLock.cs:31.
- Building at a ref: Ssdt.Build(repositoryRoot, reference, project, toolVariable, workingDirectory), io/Ssdt.cs:211-213.
- Copy.Publish (io/SqlServer.cs:194-201) runs the post-deploy seeds. CopyTests.cs:146-147 notes the seed's MERGE runs on every publish.
- The flow DriftCheck.Run follows: Standing.Of, then EnvironmentsFile.Read, then Resolve, Reach, ServerOf, Build (io/DriftCheck.cs:31-58).
- A copy's profile is chosen only inside DriftCheck's private Profile (io/DriftCheck.cs:88-95): the named one, else Environments.SharedProfile (kernel/Environments.cs:38).

Conflicts with the WP text:
- 'With drop-not-in-source': the golden pipeline profile sets DropObjectsNotInSource False (tests/Golden/project/profiles/pipeline.publish.xml). PublishProfile is closed to Strict and Permissive, which differ only in BlockOnPossibleDataLoss (io/PublishProfiles.cs:117-170; VALUES S1; CapabilityTests.Permissive_never_reaches_an_environment, :71). On a database just created the option has nothing to drop anyway.
- The WP orders 'create a database named from its fingerprints, publish, back it up'. The Facsimile builds its base in `fx_base_<hash12>_<rand4>` (ARCHITECTURE.md:229-232), a disposable name.

PAR-148 (V3_PARITY.md:249) cites `the copy build — not held yet: WP 3.5`. PAR-029 (V3_PARITY.md:143) cites `check and status — not held yet: WP 3.6`. V3_PARITY.md:290-303 (§5) words step 1 as 'the base built, published and backed up'.
items.remaining:
Smallest honest slice: no verb, and no change to the contract (cli/schemas, --help --json, cli/exits.frozen). `synthetic-copy up` is WP 3.5 as a whole; it needs WP 3.8 (pending §17 item 20) and WP 2.1's ExistingData for --existing-data.

New io/SyntheticCopy.cs, `public static class SyntheticCopy`:
- `public sealed record Base(string Key, string Backup, Reached How, Fingerprint Schema, Server Server)`, where `Reached` is a closed abstract record with the cases Built and Cached, shaped like kernel/Toolchain.cs Pin.
- `public static Stamped<Base> Of(Checkout checkout, GitRef at, string? profile, string? project, SqlServer.QueryLog log)`. Steps:
  - Standing.Of(checkout), as io/DriftCheck.cs:33-40 does.
  - The profile: lift DriftCheck.Profile (io/DriftCheck.cs:88-95) into `PublishProfiles.ForCopy(string root, Result<Environments> environmentsFile, string? named)` and use it from both.
  - Ssdt.Build(checkout.Root, at.ToString(), project, checkout.Tool, checkout.WorkingDirectory).
  - Then the inner Of.
- `internal static Result<Base> Of(string root, string dacpac, PublishProfile.Strict profile, string toolVersion, SqlServer.QueryLog log)`. Steps:
  - Ssdt.Open(dacpac). The schema is Fingerprint.Of(package.Elements.Elements).
  - LocalServer.Create(root, log): a registered disposable copy, which the sweep reaps if the run dies.
  - SqlServer.ServerOf(copy, log).
  - The key: first 16 hex of Fingerprint.Of(canonical text of schema, profile.Fingerprint, DacFx.Version, the server's version, compatibility level and image, and toolVersion).
  - FileLock.Take(state.CacheLock(key), BaseTimeout). Name BaseTimeout as Ssdt.BuildTimeout plus 10 minutes.
  - Under the lock, a hit is a marker (.json) that names the same inputs and the .bak's SHA-256. On a hit: drop the empty copy and return Cached.
  - On a miss: copy.Publish(dacpac, profile, log) under Strict as loaded. Then LocalServer.Backup(copy, state.CacheEntry(key), log). Write the marker last through Json.Text and Write.Text, as Ssdt.Build writes its marker last. Then LocalServer.Drop(copy, log) and return Built.
  - Backup's cache.unavailable becomes a note `cache.unavailable`, and the base is reported Built and uncached.
- The fingerprint-named database is the restore target of steps 2 to 8. M4's fresh copies are LocalServer.Restore(root, state.CacheEntry(key), log).

Strike or explain 'with drop-not-in-source' with a decision line. It is moot on a freshly created database, and a third profile kind contradicts VALUES S1.

Golden corpus: add tests/Golden/changes/add-a-view-over-two-tables/edits.txt. It appends `GO` and `CREATE VIEW dbo.CustomerOrders AS SELECT c.Id AS CustomerId, o.Id AS OrderId FROM dbo.Customer AS c JOIN dbo.[Order] AS o ON o.CustomerId = c.Id;` to Modules/Order.sql, after an anchor that occurs exactly once there (GoldenEdit.ApplyTo, tests/Shared/Io/GoldenProject.cs:108-115, asserts that). risks: windows-latest moved to windows-2025-vs2026 with LocalDB 17.0.4025.3 (SQL Server 2025), and the laptops run 16.x. S4 in CI measures 17.0, not 16.x, unless a job installs LocalDB 16. R5's literal '2022 only' window would refuse the Windows fixture lane outright.

A container's backup lands inside the container (/var/opt/mssql/data, written as uid 10001). Reaching .dbchange/cache/ needs docker cp in both directions, and ownership fixed so mssql can read a staged file. The alternative is a bind mount, which changes ci/sql.sh's docker run and recreates nothing already running.

A DBCHANGE_SQL server on another machine, or a Windows SQL Server service account (Msg 3201), cannot write to the repository's .dbchange/cache/. The base then has to be published from scratch every time, with a note.

io's ceiling: io is at 5,203 of 6,400. This area adds about 300 lines, and Appendix F still plans M2 at 690, M4 550, M5 670, M6 370 and M7 400, well past the remaining 1,197. A raised ceiling is the operator's decision. LocalServer.cs grows from 346 to about 500 lines; split it into a partial io/LocalServer.Cache.cs, which still satisfies CapabilityTests.Nothing_but_LocalServer_makes_a_Copy.

The sweep's 'older than a day' (VALUES O5) means a killed run's copy stays up to a day, taking LocalDB disk on laptops. The killed-run test must move the clock through an internal now parameter, because io may not use System.Diagnostics.Process to check pids.

A fingerprint-named synthetic copy has no host. Two machines on one DBCHANGE_SQL, or two clones on one machine (each with its own .dbchange/ lock), collide on the same name, and a per-checkout lock does not serialize them.

The test fixture's sweep (SqlServerFixture.cs:120-136) drops any CopyName-shaped database of this machine whose pid has ended. Any new name form must stay outside CopyName's grammar, which the hyphen in existing-data guarantees.
S4 adds roughly 1 to 3 minutes on LocalDB to a sql-windows job already at 667 s of its 20-minute limit. Installing LocalDB 16.x as well calls for a separate job or a 30-minute limit.

The probe numbers here (publish from scratch 35.3 s against restore 1.1 s for 300 tables) were taken while another fixture run shared the container. They are indicative; the decision line must cite the CI run.

The stand-in schema is built with TSqlModel and carries no post-deploy seeds. S4's publish time therefore omits the seed MERGEs the SSDT repository's real post-deploy runs; the laptop half against the real schema is a person's.
.dbchange/cache/ has no eviction. A .bak per base fingerprint accumulates across refs and DacFx or server changes.
Remedies in io name ci/sql.sh and ci/sql.ps1 (io/LocalServer.cs:189, io/SqlServer.cs:116-117, io/Doctor.cs:291), which neither the SSDT repository nor dist/dbchange/ carries.
